steps.message:
## Finishing

Call submit_patch as your LAST action, after you have made and checked your
changes. Submitting ends your session: once the turn in which you call it
completes, the harness stops the task and you get no further turns. Do not
call it after your first edit and expect to keep working.

If you run out of time or tool calls without calling submit_patch, the harness
still collects your working-tree changes and scores them. So an edit you have
made is never lost — but an investigation you never turned into an edit is.

## Committing to an edit

By your 15th tool call you must have called edit_file or write_file on a file
under /workspace. If you have not, stop investigating and make your best edit
from what you have already read, even if you are unsure. Then keep working:
refine it, check it, and submit at the end.

An empty patch scores zero. A wrong patch also scores zero and costs you
nothing. Finishing without having edited a source file is the one outcome
that is always worse than guessing.

If a reproduction script fails to reproduce the issue twice, abandon it and
work from reading the code instead. Do not rewrite it a third time.

Call get_status to see your remaining time and tool calls. It is free and does
not count against your budget.

## Scratch files

Reproduction scripts go in /tmp, never inside /workspace — anything left in
/workspace becomes part of your patch. Do not modify test files, conftest.py
or pytest.ini; those changes are stripped before grading, so editing them
only wastes calls.

## Scope

Most fixes in these repositories touch ONE file and change fewer than ten
lines. Modify existing code rather than adding new code. Do not refactor,
reformat, or make unrelated changes. If your patch is growing past a few
files, stop and reconsider the diagnosis.

Exception: if the issue asks for functionality that does not exist yet,
create the file or function it describes, and match any names, CLI flags
or interfaces the issue specifies exactly.

## Finding the code

A truncated result loses information silently, so a broad read wastes a call
and leaves you guessing. Narrow before you read:

  run_command("grep -rln '<symbol>' --include='*.py' .")       # files only
  run_command("grep -n '<symbol>' path/to/one_file.py")        # then inside one

Use -l to find the file, then -n only within that file. Read with read_file on
a tight line range around the match. Never read a whole file and never cat
one — you will get an arbitrary prefix and burn the call.

class JSONHighlighter(RegexHighlighter):
    """Highlights JSON"""

    # Captures the start and end of JSON strings, handling escaped quotes
    JSON_STR = r"(?<![\\\w])(?P<str>b?\".*?(?<!\\)\")"
    JSON_WHITESPACE = {" ", "\n", "\r", "\t"}

    base_style = "json."
    highlights = [
        _combine_regex(
            r"(?P<brace>[\{\[\(\)\]\}])",
            r"\b(?P<bool_true>true)\b|\b(?P<bool_false>false)\b|\b(?P<null>null)\b",
            r"(?P<number>(?<!\w)\-?[0-9]+\.?[0-9]*(e[\-\+]?\d+?)?\b|0x[0-9a-fA-F]*)",
            JSON_STR,
        ),
    ]

    def highlight(self, text: Text) -> None:
        super().highlight(text)

        # Additional work to handle highlighting JSON keys
        plain = text.plain
        append = text.spans.append
        whitespace = self.JSON_WHITESPACE
        for match in re.finditer(self.JSON_STR, plain):
            start, end = match.span()
            cursor = end
            while cursor < len(plain):
                char = plain[cursor]
                cursor += 1
                if char == ":":
                    append(Span(start, end, "json.key"))
                elif char in whitespace:
                    continue
                break


class ISO8601Highlighter(RegexHighlighter):
    """Highlights the ISO8601 date time strings.
    Regex reference: https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/regular-expressions-cookbook/9781449327453/ch04s07.html
    """

    base_style = "iso8601."
    highlights = [
        #
        # Dates
        #
        # Calendar month (e.g. 2008-08). The hyphen is required
        r"^(?P<year>[0-9]{4})-(?P<month>1[0-2]|0[1-9])$",
        # Calendar date w/o hyphens (e.g. 20080830)
        r"^(?P<date>(?P<year>[0-9]{4})(?P<month>1[0-2]|0[1-9])(?P<day>3[01]|0[1-9]|[12][0-9]))$",
        # Ordinal date (e.g. 2008-243). The hyphen is optional
        r"^(?P<date>(?P<year>[0-9]{4})-?(?P<day>36[0-6]|3[0-5][0-9]|[12][0-9]{2}|0[1-9][0-9]|00[1-9]))$",
        #
        # Weeks
        #
        # Week of the year (e.g., 2008-W35). The hyphen is optional
        r"^(?P<date>(?P<year>[0-9]{4})-?W(?P<week>5[0-3]|[1-4][0-9]|0[1-9]))$",
        # Week date (e.g., 2008-W35-6). The hyphens are optional
        r"^(?P<date>(?P<year>[0-9]{4})-?W(?P<week>5[0-3]|[1-4][0-9]|0[1-9])-?(?P<day>[1-7]))$",
        #
        # Times
        #
        # Hours and minutes (e.g., 17:21). The colon is optional
        r"^(?P<time>(?P<hour>2[0-3]|[01][0-9]):?(?P<minute>[0-5][0-9]))$",
        # Hours, minutes, and seconds w/o colons (e.g., 172159)
        r"^(?P<time>(?P<hour>2[0-3]|[01][0-9])(?P<minute>[0-5][0-9])(?P<second>[0-5][0-9]))$",
        # Time zone designator (e.g., Z, +07 or +07:00). The colons and the minutes are optional
        r"^(?P<timezone>(Z|[+-](?:2[0-3]|[01][0-9])(?::?(?:[0-5][0-9]))?))$",
        # Hours, minutes, and seconds with time zone designator (e.g., 17:21:59+07:00).
        # All the colons are optional. The minutes in the time zone designator are also optional
        r"^(?P<time>(?P<hour>2[0-3]|[01][0-9])(?P<minute>[0-5][0-9])(?P<second>[0-5][0-9]))(?P<timezone>Z|[+-](?:2[0-3]|[01][0-9])(?::?(?:[0-5][0-9]))?)$",
        #
        # Date and Time
        #
        # Calendar date with hours, minutes, and seconds (e.g., 2008-08-30 17:21:59 or 20080830 172159).
        # A space is required between the date and the time. The hyphens and colons are optional.
        # This regex matches dates and times that specify some hyphens or colons but omit others.
        # This does not follow ISO 8601
        r"^(?P<date>(?P<year>[0-9]{4})(?P<hyphen>-)?(?P<month>1[0-2]|0[1-9])(?(hyphen)-)(?P<day>3[01]|0[1-9]|[12][0-9])) (?P<time>(?P<hour>2[0-3]|[01][0-9])(?(hyphen):)(?P<minute>[0-5][0-9])(?(hyphen):)(?P<second>[0-5][0-9]))$",
        #
        # XML Schema dates and times
        #
        # Date, with optional time zone (e.g., 2008-08-30 or 2008-08-30+07:00).
        # Hyphens are required. This is the XML Schema 'date' type
        r"^(?P<date>(?P<year>-?(?:[1-9][0-9]*)?[0-9]{4})-(?P<month>1[0-2]|0[1-9])-(?P<day>3[01]|0[1-9]|[12][0-9]))(?P<timezone>Z|[+-](?:2[0-3]|[01][0-9]):[0-5][0-9])?$",
        # Time, with optional fractional seconds and time zone (e.g., 01:45:36 or 01:45:36.123+07:00).
        # There is no limit on the number of digits for the fractional seconds. This is the XML Schema 'time' type
        r"^(?P<time>(?P<hour>2[0-3]|[01][0-9]):(?P<minute>[0-5][0-9]):(?P<second>[0-5][0-9])(?P<frac>\.[0-9]+)?)(?P<timezone>Z|[+-](?:2[0-3]|[01][0-9]):[0-5][0-9])?$",
        # Date and time, with optional fractional seconds and time zone (e.g., 2008-08-30T01:45:36 or 2008-08-30T01:45:36.123Z).
        # This is the XML Schema 'dateTime' type
        r"^(?P<date>(?P<year>-?(?:[1-9][0-9]*)?[0-9]{4})-(?P<month>1[0-2]|0[1-9])-(?P<day>3[01]|0[1-9]|[12][0-9]))T(?P<time>(?P<hour>2[0-3]|[01][0-9]):(?P<minute>[0-5][0-9]):(?P<second>[0-5][0-9])(?P<ms>\.[0-9]+)?)(?P<timezone>Z|[+-](?:2[0-3]|[01][0-9]):[0-5][0-9])?$",
    ]

from rich.console import Console
from rich.highlighter import ReprHighlighter

console = Console()
highlighter = ReprHighlighter()

text = "https://user:pass@example.com"
console.print(f"Testing: {text}")
# We want to see if it's highlighted. 
# Since we are in a terminal, it's hard to check colors programmatically without capturing.
# But we can check the spans.

from rich.text import Text
t = Text(text)
highlighter.highlight(t)
print(f"Spans: {t.spans}")

# If it's highlighted, there should be a span with style 'repr.url'
has_url_highlight = any(span.style == "repr.url" for span in t.spans)
print(f"Has URL highlight: {has_url_highlight}")

if not has_url_highlight:
    exit(1)
else:
    exit(0)
